text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging oncall: High tail latency observed for tenant "zenith" in dedicated VPC pool eu-west-1. Trigger: tail_latency_p99 > 10s for 2m. Please check. (thread 1948000000)

melissa: I'm oncall — looking now. Are they seeing errors or just slow responses?

ingrid: CS: they report intermittent 502s and client-side timeouts. Customer is enterprise, dedicated pool. They're escalating to their SREs.

nora: quick glance at metrics — sudden jump in batch token size and per-batch memory use. A couple of nodes show repeated OOM retries.

samir: traces show long prefix processing + many concurrent long-context requests from the same tenant. Batches ballooned (max_batch_tokens reported ~4096) which is killing GPU memory compaction.

liam: infra: nodes gpu12 and gpu14 in the pool are flapping scheduler heartbeats and showing elevated compaction cycles. We're isolating them but the scheduler is still trying to pack large tenant batches.

melissa: immediate mitigation proposal: reduce zenith max_batch_tokens -> 256, cap tenant_concurrency to 8, disable burst_capacity for their queue. Any objections?

samir: +1 to minimal surface changes. Also suggest soft-limit for very large single requests later, but do the batch/ concurrency knobs first.

nora: I'll push the scheduler update now. Command I'm running:
```
rctl scheduler update --tenant zenith --set max_batch_tokens=256 --set tenant_concurrency=8
```

nora: applying change now.

runtime-bot: CHANGE_LOG: scheduler:update user=nora tenant=zenith keys=[max_batch_tokens,tenant_concurrency] old=[4096,32] new=[256,8] tx=0x7f3b

samir: watching runtime logs for effects:
```
[00:01:12] queue/zenith: observed batch_size drop 64 -> 12
[00:01:18] runtime/gpu14: gpu_mem_util reduced 98% -> 78%
[00:01:25] tail_latency_p99 reduced 11.2s -> 4.6s
```

ingrid: CS: customer reports a big improvement in response times, occasional 502s still seen but much less frequent, asking for ETA on full fix.

melissa: ok next safe mitigation: route extremely large requests to a smaller/quantized model as fallback and do a controlled canary (10% traffic for 20m) to limit impact while we debug root cause. samir can you add a routing rule?

samir: adding routing rule now:
```
routing add --tenant zenith --condition "input_tokens > 8000" --target redwood-7B-quant --pct=10 --duration=20m
```
samir: rule applied.

runtime-bot: ROUTE_CHANGE user=samir tenant=zenith route_id=rt-9a3f

liam: infra: taking gpu12 and gpu14 out of rotation for deeper investigation to avoid noisy neighbor effects.

nora: telemetry: p99 now ~2.1s, p95 ~350ms. Improvements look stable for last 6m.

melissa: keeping page open until stable for 30m. Action items for follow-up: 1) propose default per-tenant max_batch_tokens cap (e.g., 1024) and alert when per-tenant batch_size > 64 sustained >1m; 2) examine client-side patterns causing huge batches (fanout/single session multiplexing); 3) consider streaming/segmentation fallback for >4096 tokens.

ingrid: I'll coordinate with Zenith account team and offer an optional maintenance window so we can apply permanent throttles with customer consent.

samir: notes for eng: investigate why scheduler allowed large batches when dedicated pool nodes were degrading — possible autoscaler interplay or delayed eviction. Also add a safety path to convert gigantic single requests into chunked streaming where semantics allow.

melissa: handing off monitoring to night oncall @nora at 1948000300. I'll add detailed notes to incident doc. Thanks all — great quick work.

nora: ack, taking over. leaving incident notes at https://redwood.internal/incidents/INC-1948000000

incident-bot: Reminder: incident not auto-closed. Please mark resolved when postmortem actions scheduled.

melissa: marking incident as acknowledged/resolved for now. We'll run a short post-incident review tomorrow and follow up with the customer on permanent config. :white_check_mark:

-- end of thread --
